answer: To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 11 epochs old, anchored at a cipher checkpoint. The pulse chain is verified at intake and ridge publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 11 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. The attacker spends 236 dollars and 10 days per identity before it can vote at all. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
